## Catalog Description

Probability for Engineering Decisions. (3-0). Credit 3. Introduction to probability and stochastic processes for characterization of uncertainty in engineering decisions. Prerequisite: Approval of instructor.

## Course Learning Outcomes

Upon completion of this course, the learner will be able to:

- Use tools and techniques from probability theory to characterize uncertainty in engineering decisions

## Special Course Designation

None

## Grading Policy

- Grading Scale: A = 90-100%, B = 80-89%, C = 70-79%, D = 60-69%, F = <60%.

- Weights: Assignments 20%, First exam 40%, Second exam 40%, Homework 0%.

- Assignments: no make-ups; take-home, open notes/book.

- First exam: in-class, closed-notes on October 22, 2026

- Second exam: non-cumulative, in-class, closed-notes on December 3, 2026

- Homework: Not collected; solutions will be given. Spend time solving the homework problems. Do not peek into the solutions too early. The homework problems have a programming component; implementing analytical concepts in software is crucial for their understanding.

- Grading appeals: Every effort will be made to ensure that grading is as objective and fair as possible. If you believe that there is an error in the grading, please submit, in writing, an appeal within one week of your work being returned. However, please be advised that if you submit such an appeal, the entire assignment/exam will be regraded to ensure that all parts are properly graded. As such, your grade on the exam could increase or decrease based on the secondary grading.

## Late Work Policy

Work submitted by a student as makeup work for an excused absence is not considered late work and is exempt from the late work policy (Student Rule 7).

## Course Specific Late Work Policy

Work submitted after a deadline is considered late and will not be accepted.

## Course Schedule

Week

Topics

1-3

Review of basic probability (probability spaces and axioms;

conditional probability and dependence; law of total

probability and Beyes rule; random variables, distributions

and expectation operator; multivariate distributions;

computation of expectations; linearity of expectation)

4-7

Discrete-time Markov chains (modeling, transient analysis

and classification of states, steady-state analysis, balance

equations, Monte Carlo Markov chain)

9

First exam (October 22, 2026)

7, 8, 10

Dynamic programming (finite-horizon problems, infinite-

horizon discounted problems, value iteration and synthesis

of optimal policy, policy iteration)

11-13

Continuous-time Markov chains (exponential distribution,

modeling, Poisson process and its properties, transient

analysis and classification of states, steady-state analysis,

embedded chain)

15

Second exam (December 3, 2026)
